close_reason: Added one comprehensive extras-stress test (email_extras_multi_field_nested_and_string_roundtrip) on the canonical Email type, covering all three gaps identified in the finding: (1) multiple vendor fields on the same object, (2) nested-object + nested-array structural extras, (3) byte-level to_string/from_str roundtrip (not just to_value/from_value). One test on the canonical extension-types template (Email per workspace AGENTS.md) implicitly validates the same serde-flatten + Map<String, Value> machinery used by every cookie-cut sibling, avoiding test multiplication across 30+ types. Test uses hand-written JSON as oracle. All tests + clippy pass.
description:
Each in-scope type added a single round-trip test of the form:

```rust
let raw = json!({ /* required fields */, "acmeCorpFoo": "bar" });
let val: Type = serde_json::from_value(raw).unwrap();
assert_eq!(val.extra.get("acmeCorpFoo").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some("bar"));
let back = serde_json::to_value(&val).unwrap();
assert_eq!(back["acmeCorpFoo"], "bar");
```

This is a good baseline but leaves three real round-trip-correctness gaps uncovered:

(1) **Multiple extras on the same object.** None of the tests put two unknown keys (e.g. `acmeCorpFoo` and `siteBar`) on the same object. If serde's flatten implementation has any single-key happy-path bias, a two-key bug would slip past.

(2) **Nested-object extras with structural depth.** Tests use scalar or one-level-deep values. A vendor field like `{"acmeCorpSchema": {"version": 2, "signed": [{"by": "x"}]}}` exercises serde_json::Map<String, Value>'s recursive round-trip. The Email test in email.rs:509 has `acmeCorpClassification: { label, score }` — one level deep, no arrays. No test exercises a deeper nested array.

(3) **JSON-string round-trip (not just Value).** Every test uses `serde_json::from_value(raw)` and `serde_json::to_value(&val)`. None go through the actual byte-level `from_str`/`to_string` pipeline. `from_value` skips the tokenizer entirely — if the flatten+Map combination interacts badly with the streaming deserializer's buffering, the Value-only test would not catch it.

The `email_address_empty_extras_omitted_from_wire` test at email.rs:526 partially covers the empty-extras case but only for one type and uses `to_value` not `to_string`.

Fix scope: add one negative-control test per file that exercises all three gaps:
- two unknown fields on the same object
- one nested-array extra
- round-trip through `serde_json::to_string` → `from_str` → `to_string` and assert byte-for-byte equality on the second serialization (canonical form, accounting for HashMap key order non-determinism)

The 'one round-trip preservation test per migrated type' rule documented in PLAN.md is satisfied today but is the floor, not the ceiling. The gap matters because every extension-types sibling will cookie-cut from this canonical template — a thin test layer here propagates to seven downstream crates.

Bikeshedding-vs-real check: this is a real coverage gap for a documented workspace policy. The mechanical addition of `extra` fields is unverified against the three cases above; if serde-flatten + Map had any known bug touching one of them (and historically serde-flatten has had several round-trip bugs around `null`, untagged enums, and Map-as-flatten-target), the workspace would not notice until production. Not bikeshedding — but P2 not P0 because every existing test still passes and the workspace policy is mechanically sound.
title: Extras-preservation tests cover only single-field shallow extras — gap on multi-field, nested, and JSON-string round-trip cases
